title: Working Over or Near Water
summary: Falling into water can be fatal, even for good swimmers. OSHA requires life jackets, inspected gear, ring buoys and a rescue skiff when the danger of drowning exists.
talking_points: Workers working over or next to water, where there is a danger of drowning, must be provided with a U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket or buoyant work vest (29 CFR 1926.106(a)).
Inspect life jackets, buoyant work vests and life preservers before and after each use for defects that would change their strength or buoyancy. Do not use one with a defect (1926.106(b)).
Keep ring buoys with at least 90 feet of line ready for rescue, and do not space them more than 200 feet apart (1926.106(c)).
At least one lifesaving skiff must be immediately available at locations over or next to water (1926.106(d)).
Good practice: know before you start where the buoys and skiff are and who will use them.
Good practice: never work near water alone, and agree on how you will call for help.
site_hazards_to_check: Work over or next to water with no life jackets issued
Life jacket or vest that is damaged or has lost buoyancy
No ring buoy within reach, or buoys spaced more than 200 feet apart
Ring buoy with less than 90 feet of line
discussion_questions: Where are the life jackets, ring buoys and skiff on this job?
How do you check a life jacket before you put it on?
Who rescues a worker who falls in, and how quickly can they reach them?
